narrative:
The model estimates a 44% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three factors stood out most in this decision. First, the number of training programs you attended in the last three years pushed the prediction strongly toward staying. You completed seven or more, far above the average among employees the model expects to remain. This signals strong engagement and development potential.

However, two experience-related factors pulled the prediction in the opposite direction and ultimately outweighed the training benefit. Your six to ten years of total professional experience is higher than most people the model predicts will stay, yet your relatively short time with this current organization—one to five years—suggests you may still be evaluating whether this role is the right long-term fit. The model interprets this combination as an elevated risk of departure.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals openly with you and exploring ways to strengthen your sense of belonging in the education sector. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether additional time in this role or further internal opportunities could change your outlook. Addressing these points early could still turn the situation around.
